title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-23
content:
Purpose:
Notes / breadcrumbs for a recurring edge-case: requests hitting sequence-length boundary (~2048) cause attention kernel selection to fall back from flash-attn (fast path) to aten/unpadded kernel, which sometimes triggers downstream KV-cache mis-indexing and a small % of 5xxs or incorrect completions. Working notes, commands I ran, error snippets and hypotheses.

High-level symptom:
- Intermittent correctness/regression observed in production traces for long prompts (~2048 tokens).
- When client concat/truncation results in sequence length exactly at/one-over model config boundary (2048 / 2049), runtime picks non-flash kernel.
- Non-flash path sometimes yields a KV cache miss (indexes shift) - generation diverges.
- Repro locally with synthetic inputs (see steps below).

Repro steps I used (local docker dev image rt-dev:latest):
1) baseline reproducer (python script):
   python debug/repro_seqlen_edgecase.py --model redwood-ggml-7b --input-file tests/data/long_prompt_2048.txt

2) quick CLI runs to exercise kernel selection trace:
   export RW_DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTION=1
   export RW_ENABLE_FLASH_ATTENTION=1
   python -m rt.server --run-once --trace-kernel-selection

3) single-request curl (simulate gateway):
   curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-ggml-7b","prompt":"<long-prompt-2048-tokens>","max_tokens":64}'

4) batch request (2 requests packed, different seqlen):
   python tools/batch_sim.py --requests "[r1.json,r2.json]" --batch_size 2 --combine_strategy prefix

Observed logs / snippets:
- Kernel selection trace (from --trace-kernel-selection):
  [INFO] selected kernel=flash_attn_unpadded  for seq_len=2032, batch=1, kv-cached=false
  [INFO] selected kernel=flash_attn_unpadded  for seq_len=2048, batch=1, kv-cached=false
  [INFO] selected kernel=aten_attn_nonbatched (fallback) for seq_len=2049, reason=seqlen-pad-mismatch

- Error seen in one run after fallback: (shortened)
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "rt/inference/dispatch.py", line 412, in run_forward
      attn_out = kernel.run(q, k, v, seqlen=seq_len)
    File "rt/inference/kernels/aten_attn.py", line 87, in run
      assert k.shape[2] == seq_len, f"seq_length mismatch: expected {seq_len} got {k.shape[2]}"
  AssertionError: seq_length mismatch: expected 2049 got 2048

- Another failure variant (GPU crash) when forcing flash-attn (env var RW_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn):
  cudaGetLastError() -> invalid configuration argument
  kernel launch failed: flash_attn_smem_kernel.cu:line 256
  NOTE: only on sm80 with driver 530.x, not reproduced on sm86 test nodes.

- Sample of produced (incorrect) output vs expected (diff):
  expected: "...as a result, the function returns SUCCESS and the logits stabilize."
  actual:   "...as a result, the function returns FAIL and the logits changed."

Hypotheses / theories:
1) kernel selection logic uses per-request seqlen but does not account for combined KV cache length when using cached key/value (i.e., runtime compares only current chunk length vs flash threshold). That leads to choosing flash for a chunk but kernel expects a different padding layout.
2) Batch packing: when two requests with different seqlen are batched, padding calculation across the batch is inconsistent between kernel selection and the KV cache write/read ordering. Result: k/v indexing off by pad amount.
3) A race between KV cache update and attention kernel invocation when fallback path chosen - maybe an off-by-one index when writing newly-attended tokens into the KV cache.
4) Driver/kernel mismatch: forcing flash-attn on sm80 triggers invalid config due to block/thread configuration assumptions (we need to validate minimum compute capability and driver).

Experiments & results so far:
- Add extra invariant checks in kernels/aten_attn.py to validate k/v shapes before read/write: saw assertion hits that match above mismatch.
- Reproduced deterministic mismatch with synthetic single-run that appends one token at a time until 2049 boundary; kernel assertion fires reliably.
- Running same synthetic on sm86 machine (internal-test-2) did NOT crash on flash-attn forced - suggests driver or sm arch difference.
- When I disable batching (FORCE_NO_BATCH=1), the error rate drops to ~0.1% from 1.9% on local cluster during the same load.
- Adding a 1-token pad to all inputs (pad to nearest > flash threshold) makes runtime consistently pick aten path and avoids the mismatch, but performance regresses.

Quick notes on code areas to inspect:
- rt/inference/kernel_selector.py -> selection heuristics & boundary conditions
- rt/cache/kv_store.py -> write ordering & offsets when merging new KV with existing cache
- rt/inference/kernels/flash_attn_bridge.py  -> padding assumptions & launch config
- rt/inference/kernels/aten_attn.py -> current asserts and shape checks (I added ensures here temporarily)

Service traces / breadcrumbs (prod-ish):
- trace ids: trace-20251106-1a2b3c (payload ~2049 tokens) -> kernel=aten fallback -> downstream delta in tokens -> user ticket #1257
- trace-20251214-0f0e1d (batch of 3) -> mixed kernel selection across batch boundary -> 502 spike correlates

Immediate next steps (short-term):
- Add better logging where kernel selection reasons include "kv_cached" and "combined_seq_len" (currently selection only prints reason=seqlen-pad-mismatch)
- Unit test: add reproducer that simulates existing cache length N and new chunk length M where N+M crosses flash threshold and assert selection/fallback behavior is deterministic and that KV read/write offsets align. Put test under tests/serving/test_kernel_selection.py::test_kv_boundary
- Validate on CI matrix: run repro on sm80 with driver 530.x and sm86 with driver 540.x to capture differences. Add GPU-matrix label to CI job.
- Short term mitigation: when patching is risky, add a temporary runtime guard: if kernel selection would flip between flash and aten for same request between planning and dispatch, force aten (safe) and emit metric (kv_kernel_fallback_forced).
- Longer term: rework selection to compute "effective_seq_len = existing_kv_len + chunk_len" and select kernel against effective length; ensure kernels get consistent pad info.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Ask @Miguel to repro on his sm80-test node (driver 530.12) and paste kernel launch logs.
- Follow up with flash-attn upstream (fork/issue) about block config and sm80 edgecases.
- Check recent change in PR #4123 (linked) for selection heuristics - probably introduced last-quarter.
- Add more instrumentation to the KV write path (temporary) to log offsets & lengths for a sampling of requests. Keep sampling low (0.1%) to avoid cost.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the mismatch due to an off-by-one in how we append new kv entries (i.e., we reserve slot for BOS/EOS differently across kernels)?
- Are there any older models/specs that use different seq_len semantics (e.g., they count prompt tokens differently) that would change effective length?

If I get time today:
- implement the effective_seq_len computation in kernel_selector + unit test (local PR).
- push a small metric for kernel flip and enable logging sampling.

End of notes.
(If lost: see repro scripts in debug/ and my test runs in /tmp/rt-repro-20251105/ )
